Job 2 — Ground-truth retrieval: qualitative figure

This job produces the figure that shows what our method predicts, touch by touch, on the ground-truth-retrieval benchmark. "Ground-truth retrieval" means the correct reference touch is handed to the method, so the figure isolates the two stages we care about here: the coarse alignment by feature matching, and the refinement network that cleans it up.

What was run

RetrievalGround truth — on this benchmark query touch i is rendered at the same location as reference touch i, so the pairing is the identity map (log/touch_retrieval, built with --retrieval_mode tsv). DINOv3 similarity search is what the full-pipeline benchmark exercises instead.
Coarse alignmentSuperPoint keypoints + SuperGlue matching on the surface normal renders at 4x the sensor footprint, followed by a median translation offset (main_retrieval_transfer_feat_match.py --modality normal --match_scale 25 --match_scale_convention obj_scale_factor)
Refinement networkReBotNet-S with the query normal map concatenated to the input and sinusoidal temporal FiLM — log/rebot_checkpoints_S_geomcat_film/best.pth, epoch 18
Evaluated on50 held-out objects (951–1000), 400 touch locations, 50 frames each
Hardwareone RTX 2080 Ti

The figure

How to read the tactile images. They are surface-normal maps: the colour of a pixel encodes which way the gel surface is tilted at that point. Flat, untouched gel is the uniform light blue-violet; a ridge or edge pressing into the gel shows up as a sharp colour change.

How much the refinement network helps

Averaged over all 400 evaluation touches and all 50 frames of each touch. PSNR and SSIM are higher-is-better; LPIPS and MSE are lower-is-better.

StagePSNR (dB)SSIMLPIPSMSE
Coarse transfer (feature matching only)22.930.83480.21050.0166
Refined transfer (ours, refinement network)31.280.92280.10750.0054

The refinement network adds +8.35 dB of PSNR on top of the coarse alignment.

These are our method's numbers only. The comparison against the baselines (Tactile Normal Quilting, implicit neural representations, TaRF) is a separate job that runs on the other machine; this table is the "ours" row of that comparison, computed here because the coarse transfer had to be run locally anyway.

Matching modality: normals vs curvature

The experiment plan asks for the surface normal renders as the matching modality, but the script it points at (train_refine_scripts/transfer_all_real_data_gt_retrieval_tactile_normal/) passes --transfer_modality curvature. Both were run end to end over the same 400 touches so the choice is settled by measurement. Normals is the default used above.

Matching modalityCoarse PSNRRefined PSNR Refined SSIMRefined LPIPS
Normals (default)22.93 31.28 0.92280.1075
Curvature22.74 31.20 0.9214 0.1100
The two are statistically indistinguishable here. Normals is nominally ahead on every metric (+0.08 dB refined, +0.20 dB coarse), but the paired per-touch difference has a median of exactly zero — on many touches the matcher converges to the same transform — normals wins on only 194/400 touches after refinement, and a Wilcoxon signed-rank test does not reject equality (p = 0.21 refined, p = 0.54 coarse). So "normals at 4x" is the stated default, not a demonstrated advantage; the ablation study will report this axis properly.

Where the assets are

  • log/paper_job02_gt_retrieval_figure_normalmatch/ — the default (normals) run: figure, per-cell assets, per-touch metrics
  • log/paper_job02_gt_retrieval_figure/ — the curvature run, same layout
  • <run>/assets/<object>_<touch>_0N_*.png — every individual cell, at full resolution, for all 400 touches (not just the three shown). For the touches used in the figure, the normal renders are additionally saved at all three fields of view (..._scale100/50/25.png = 1x / 2x / 4x), each with a _box variant carrying the red 1x-footprint outline
  • log/paper_job02_gt_retrieval_figure/per_touch_metrics.pkl — per-touch metrics
  • paper_experiments/02_gt_retrieval_figure/ — the scripts and the Markdown fact sheet
